name: ACCESS
aliases: Abdominal Colpopexy: Comparison of Endoscopic Surgical Strategies
question: How do robotic and conventional laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy compare in cost and clinical outcomes for apical prolapse?

design.blinding: not reported in the primary report
design.population: Seventy-eight women at two academic centers had symptomatic stage II or greater pelvic organ prolapse with substantial apical descent and an indication for sacrocolpopexy.
design.description: Two-center randomized comparative effectiveness surgical trial
design.locator: Anger 2014, Materials and Methods; Results, paragraph 1

verdictNote: Robotic hospital costs were higher; clinical comparisons were secondary and underpowered.
takeaway: ACCESS randomized robotic versus conventional laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy and found higher hospital costs with robotics through six weeks, largely from robot purchase and maintenance; clinical outcomes were secondary.

reports.label: Cost and six-month outcomes
reports.citation: Anger JT, Mueller ER, Tarnay C, et al. "Robotic compared with laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy: a randomized controlled trial." *Obstet Gynecol.* 2014;123(1):5-12. doi:10.1097/AOG.0000000000000006
reports.followUp: Six weeks for the primary cost outcome; six months for prolapse outcomes
reports.followUpLocator: Anger 2014, Materials and Methods; Results, clinical outcomes paragraph

results.endpoint: Total hospital costs through six weeks
results.measure: Mean six-week hospital cost; mean difference in US dollars (robotic minus laparoscopic)
results.note: Includes robot purchase and maintenance; the power calculation used total charges: 32 per arm gave 95% power to detect a $2,500 difference at a two-sided alpha of 0.05.
results.locator: Anger 2014, Table 2, Total 6-week costs; Materials and Methods, statistical analysis

results.measure: Mean day-of-surgery hospital cost; mean difference in US dollars (robotic minus laparoscopic)
results.locator: Anger 2014, Table 2, Day of surgery costs

results.endpoint: Six-week costs excluding robot purchase and maintenance
results.measure: Mean six-week hospital cost; mean difference in US dollars (robotic minus laparoscopic)
results.note: Sensitivity analysis excluding robot capital and maintenance costs.
results.locator: Anger 2014, Table 2, Total 6-week costs excluding robotics

results.measure: Mean Surgical Pain Scale score at one week; mean difference in points (robotic minus laparoscopic)
results.note: Secondary recovery outcome; difference diminished by two weeks.

results.measure: Mean POP-Q point C in cm at six months
results.note: P is the table's treatment-effect comparison; the study was powered for cost, not prolapse outcomes.

harms.label: Adverse-event counts and severity

values.exp: 6 events: 1 Dindo I, 2 II, 2 III, 1 IV

harms.note: Counts are events, not affected patients; indexed severity-and-count comparison P=0.868.

harms.label: Selected operative and postoperative complications

values.exp: 1 iliac venotomy; 1 bowel obstruction requiring exploration; 1 pulmonary embolism
values.ctl: 1 iliac venotomy; 1 bowel obstruction; 1 port-site hernia requiring reoperation; 1 intraoperative cystotomy

harms.note: Both venotomies were closed intraoperatively without changing access route; three laparoscopic cases had vaginal granulation tissue or suture exposure.

delivery.label: Surgeon experience and centers
delivery.value: Five surgeons at UCLA/Cedars-Sinai and Loyola had each performed at least 10 robotic and 10 laparoscopic sacrocolpopexies before study participation.
delivery.locator: Anger 2014, Materials and Methods, entry criteria and surgeon experience; Results, paragraph 1

delivery.label: Operative technique
delivery.value: Two separate synthetic-mesh pieces and Gore-Tex sutures were used in both arms; mesh brand and reperitonealization were at surgeon discretion.
delivery.locator: Anger 2014, Materials and Methods, operative paragraph

delivery.label: Concomitant surgery
delivery.value: 45/78 women (58%) underwent hysterectomy, 47/78 (60%) retropubic midurethral sling, and 5/78 (6%) anterior or posterior repair.
delivery.locator: Anger 2014, Table 1, Concurrent procedures at surgery

delivery.label: Sacrocolpopexy procedure time
delivery.note: Difference 24.4 minutes (P=0.030); total surgery time did not differ significantly.

reports.label: One-year patient and anatomic outcomes
reports.citation: Kenton K, Mueller ER, Tarney C, Bresee C, Anger JT. "One-year outcomes after minimally invasive sacrocolpopexy." *Female Pelvic Med Reconstr Surg.* 2016;22(5):382-384. doi:10.1097/SPV.0000000000000300

results.measure: Patient Global Impression of Improvement at one year among assessed women
results.note: Planned ancillary analysis; 'improved' meant very much better or much better.

results.measure: Mean POP-Q point C in cm at one year

harms.label: Sacrocolpopexy mesh complication or mesh-exposure reoperation by one year
harms.note: One asymptomatic Gore-Tex suture erosion occurred, arm unspecified; three bowel-related reoperations occurred within the first six to eight weeks, arms unspecified in this report.

relations.note: Both randomized robotic versus laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy and found greater robotic cost; Paraiso's primary endpoint was operative time.
